name: Null Signal: Shelf Edition
description: A pirate mesh broadcast running out of the Shelf's lower stack, airing three times a week at randomized intervals to avoid signal triangulation. Hosted by an anonymous collective using the shared handle 'Orin,' the show combines investigative reporting on corponation security movements, practical segments on disabling standard-issue compliance collars, and a rotating community bulletin that functions as a survival network for unregistered residents. Audio quality is intentionally degraded to mask voice signatures, and the visual feed is a smeared thermal overlay that makes faces unrecognizable.
cultural_impact: The compliance collar disabling segment — nicknamed 'the Orin trick' — spread to Shelf communities across three districts and reduced corponation security's behavioral monitoring efficiency by an estimated 11%.
story_hooks: A player is approached by someone claiming to be the original 'Orin' — before the collective took the name — who says the current broadcast has been compromised.
HelixCorp Security is running a honeypot operation using a fake mesh node that mimics the Null Signal feed.
The community bulletin contains a coded message that only makes sense if you know a specific dead drop location — and someone very dangerous is already on their way there.
